questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM PH Topic • Electricity and Magnetism (Set 02)
questions.questionTextEn: A thin wire carrying steady current $I$ is bent into a semicircular arc of radius $R$. The magnitude of the magnetic field at the center of curvature due to the semicircular arc alone is
questions.explanationEn: For a circular arc subtending angle $\theta$ at its center, $B = \frac{\mu_0 I \theta}{4\pi R}$. For a semicircle ($\theta = \pi$), $B = \frac{\mu_0 I}{4R}$.

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM PH Topic • Electricity and Magnetism (Set 02)
questions.questionTextEn: A point charge $q$ is placed at one corner of a cube of side $a$. The total electric flux passing through any one of the three faces of the cube that do NOT touch that corner is
questions.explanationEn: Eight identical cubes meet at the corner to enclose $q$ symmetrically, so the total flux through the single cube is $\frac{q}{8\varepsilon_0}$. The three faces touching the corner have zero flux (field is parallel to them), so the remaining three faces share $\frac{q}{8\varepsilon_0}$ equally, giving $\frac{q}{24\varepsilon_0}$ per face.

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM PH Topic • Electricity and Magnetism (Set 02)
questions.questionTextEn: An isolated parallel-plate capacitor carries charge $Q$ and stores electrostatic energy $U_0$. A linear dielectric slab of relative permittivity $\varepsilon_r = 4$ is then inserted to completely fill the space between the plates. The new stored electrostatic energy is
questions.explanationEn: Because the capacitor is isolated, the charge $Q$ remains constant while the capacitance increases to $C = \varepsilon_r C_0 = 4C_0$. Hence $U = \frac{Q^2}{2C} = \frac{U_0}{4}$.

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM PH Topic • Electricity and Magnetism (Set 02)
questions.questionTextEn: A conducting rod of length $L$ rotates with constant angular velocity $\omega$ about one of its ends in a plane perpendicular to a uniform magnetic field $B$. The magnitude of the induced emf between the two ends of the rod is
questions.explanationEn: Integrating $d\mathcal{E} = B v\,dr = B(\omega r)\,dr$ from $r = 0$ to $r = L$ gives $\mathcal{E} = \int_0^L B\omega r\,dr = \frac{1}{2}B\omega L^2$.

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM PH Topic • Electricity and Magnetism (Set 02)
questions.questionTextEn: Two small coaxial magnetic dipoles $\vec{m}_1 = m_1\hat{z}$ and $\vec{m}_2 = m_2\hat{z}$ are separated by a large distance $z$ along the $z$-axis. The magnitude of the magnetic force between them varies with separation $z$ as
questions.explanationEn: The axial magnetic field of dipole $1$ is $B_z(z) = \frac{\mu_0 m_1}{2\pi z^3}$. The interaction potential energy is $U = -\vec{m}_2\cdot\vec{B}_1 = -\frac{\mu_0 m_1 m_2}{2\pi z^3}$, so the force is $F_z = -\frac{dU}{dz} = -\frac{3\mu_0 m_1 m_2}{2\pi z^4} \propto \frac{1}{z^4}$.

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM PH Topic • Electricity and Magnetism (Set 02)
questions.questionTextEn: A long solid cylindrical wire of radius $R$ carries an axial current whose current density varies radially as $\vec{J}(r) = k r\hat{z}$, where $k$ is a positive constant. The magnitude of the magnetic field at an interior radial distance $r < R$ is
questions.explanationEn: The enclosed current within radius $r$ is $I_{\text{enc}} = \int_0^r (kr')(2\pi r'\,dr') = \frac{2\pi k r^3}{3}$. By Ampère's law, $B(2\pi r) = \mu_0 I_{\text{enc}} \implies B(r) = \frac{\mu_0 k r^2}{3}$.

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM PH Topic • Electricity and Magnetism (Set 02)
questions.questionTextEn: The magnetic field of a plane electromagnetic wave propagating in vacuum is given by $\vec{B}(z, t) = B_0\cos(kz - \omega t)\hat{y}$. The corresponding electric field $\vec{E}(z, t)$ is
questions.explanationEn: The wave propagates along $\hat{k} = +\hat{z}$. In vacuum, $\vec{E} = -c(\hat{k}\times\vec{B}) = -c(\hat{z}\times\hat{y})B_0\cos(kz - \omega t) = +c B_0\cos(kz - \omega t)\hat{x}$.

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM PH Topic • Electricity and Magnetism (Set 02)
questions.questionTextEn: A uniform magnetic field $\vec{B}(t) = \alpha t\hat{z}$ (with $\alpha > 0$) is confined to a long cylindrical region of radius $R$ centered on the $z$-axis. The magnitude of the induced electric field at a radial distance $r < R$ from the axis is
questions.explanationEn: By Faraday's law on a circular loop of radius $r < R$, $E(2\pi r) = \frac{d}{dt}(\pi r^2 \alpha t) = \pi r^2 \alpha \implies E = \frac{\alpha r}{2}$.

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM PH Topic • Electricity and Magnetism (Set 02)
questions.questionTextEn: A conducting rod of mass $m$ and length $L$ slides without friction down two vertical conducting rails connected at the top by a resistor $R$. A uniform horizontal magnetic field $B$ is directed perpendicular to the plane of the rails. Neglecting rail and rod resistance, the terminal speed of the rod is
questions.explanationEn: At speed $v$, the motional emf is $\mathcal{E} = BLv$, driving current $I = \frac{BLv}{R}$ and producing an upward magnetic braking force $F_B = ILB = \frac{B^2 L^2 v}{R}$. At terminal velocity, $F_B = mg \implies v_t = \frac{mgR}{B^2 L^2}$.

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM PH Topic • Electricity and Magnetism (Set 02)
questions.questionTextEn: An air-filled parallel-plate capacitor of plate area $A$ and separation $d$ carries charges $+Q$ and $-Q$ on its plates. Which of the following statements is/are correct?
optionsEn: If the separation $d$ is doubled while connected to a constant-voltage battery, the stored energy is halved
The magnitude of the attractive force between the two plates is $F = \frac{Q^2}{2\varepsilon_0 A}$
The attractive force between the plates equals $Q E_{\text{gap}}$, where $E_{\text{gap}} = \frac{Q}{\varepsilon_0 A}$ is the total field between the plates
If the separation $d$ is doubled while the capacitor is isolated (constant $Q$), the stored energy doubles
questions.explanationEn: Each plate produces field $\frac{Q}{2\varepsilon_0 A}$, so the force on the other plate is $F = \frac{Q^2}{2\varepsilon_0 A} = \frac{1}{2}QE_{\text{gap}}$ (first True, fourth False). At constant $Q$, $U = \frac{Q^2 d}{2\varepsilon_0 A} \propto d$ doubles when $d$ doubles (True). At constant $V$, $U = \frac{\varepsilon_0 A V^2}{2d} \propto 1/d$ halves when $d$ doubles (True).

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM PH Topic • Electricity and Magnetism (Set 02)
questions.questionTextEn: In a Wheatstone bridge consisting of four resistors $R_1, R_2, R_3, R_4$ with a galvanometer of resistance $R_g$ connected between the midpoints and a DC source across the other two corners, which of the following statements is/are correct when the bridge is balanced?
optionsEn: $R_1 R_4 = R_2 R_3$ (for $R_1, R_2$ in the upper arms and $R_3, R_4$ in the lower arms)
The balance condition depends on the internal resistance of the DC source
Interchanging the battery and the galvanometer preserves the balance condition
Zero current flows through the galvanometer branch
questions.explanationEn: At balance, the two midpoint nodes are at equal potential, giving $R_1/R_2 = R_3/R_4 \iff R_1 R_4 = R_2 R_3$, zero galvanometer current, and symmetry under swapping source and detector (first three True). The balance condition is purely a resistance ratio and is independent of the source emf or internal resistance (False).

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM PH Topic • Electricity and Magnetism (Set 02)
questions.questionTextEn: Consider two fixed rigid conducting coils $1$ and $2$ in vacuum with self-inductances $L_1, L_2$ and mutual inductance $M$. Which of the following statements is/are correct?
optionsEn: When currents $I_1$ and $I_2$ flow in the coils, the total stored magnetic energy is $U_B = \frac{1}{2}L_1 I_1^2 + \frac{1}{2}L_2 I_2^2 \pm M I_1 I_2$
By Neumann's reciprocity theorem, $M_{12} = M_{21} = M$
The self-inductance $L_1$ depends on the magnitude of the current $I_1$ flowing through coil $1$
The mutual inductance always satisfies $|M| \le \sqrt{L_1 L_2}$
questions.explanationEn: Neumann's formula guarantees $M_{12} = M_{21} = M$, energy positivity $U_B \ge 0$ guarantees $|M| \le \sqrt{L_1 L_2}$, and $U_B = \frac{1}{2}L_1 I_1^2 + \frac{1}{2}L_2 I_2^2 \pm M I_1 I_2$ (all three True). In vacuum (linear medium), $L_1$ is purely geometrical and independent of $I_1$ (False).

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM PH Topic • Electricity and Magnetism (Set 02)
questions.questionTextEn: Poynting's theorem in differential form is written as $\frac{\partial u}{\partial t} + \nabla\cdot\vec{S} = -\vec{J}\cdot\vec{E}$, where $u = \frac{1}{2}\left(\varepsilon_0 E^2 + \frac{B^2}{\mu_0}\right)$ and $\vec{S} = \frac{1}{\mu_0}(\vec{E}\times\vec{B})$. Which of the following statements is/are correct?
optionsEn: For static, crossed uniform electric and magnetic fields in vacuum, $\vec{S}$ is always identically zero
$\vec{S}$ represents the electromagnetic energy flux density (power per unit area) in $\text{W/m}^2$
For a steady Ohmic current in a straight cylindrical resistor, $\vec{S}$ at the wire surface points radially inward, supplying the Joule heat dissipated inside
The electromagnetic momentum density stored in free-space fields is $\vec{g} = \frac{\vec{S}}{c^2} = \varepsilon_0(\vec{E}\times\vec{B})$
questions.explanationEn: $\vec{S}$ is energy flux density in $\text{W/m}^2$, field momentum density is $\vec{g} = \vec{S}/c^2$, and in a DC resistor $\vec{E}$ is axial and $\vec{B}$ is azimuthal so $\vec{S}$ points radially inward (first three True). Static crossed $\vec{E}$ and $\vec{B}$ fields have $\vec{S} = \frac{1}{\mu_0}(\vec{E}\times\vec{B}) \neq \vec{0}$ (though $\nabla\cdot\vec{S} = 0$) (False).

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM PH Topic • Electricity and Magnetism (Set 02)
questions.questionTextEn: Two nearby coils have a mutual inductance of $0.25\text{ H}$. If the current in the primary coil changes at a steady rate of $40\text{ A/s}$, the magnitude of the emf induced in the secondary coil is ______ $\text{V}$. (Answer in integer)
questions.explanationEn: By definition of mutual inductance, $|\mathcal{E}_2| = M\left|\frac{dI_1}{dt}\right| = 0.25 \times 40 = 10\text{ V}$.

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM PH Topic • Electricity and Magnetism (Set 02)
questions.questionTextEn: A collimated beam of electromagnetic radiation with average intensity $1500\text{ W/m}^2$ falls normally on a perfectly absorbing black plate. Taking $c = 3 \times 10^8\text{ m/s}$, the radiation pressure exerted on the plate is ______ $\mu\text{Pa}$. (Answer in integer)
questions.explanationEn: For normal incidence on a perfectly absorbing surface, $P_{\text{rad}} = \frac{I}{c} = \frac{1500}{3 \times 10^8} = 5 \times 10^{-6}\text{ Pa} = 5\ \mu\text{Pa}$.

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM PH Topic • Electricity and Magnetism (Set 02)
questions.questionTextEn: A series $RL$ circuit has an inductance of $60\text{ mH}$ and a total resistance of $15\ \Omega$. Its inductive time constant is ______ $\text{ms}$. (Answer in integer)
questions.explanationEn: The $RL$ time constant is $\tau = \frac{L}{R} = \frac{60 \times 10^{-3}\text{ H}}{15\ \Omega} = 4 \times 10^{-3}\text{ s} = 4\text{ ms}$.

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM PH Topic • Electricity and Magnetism (Set 02)
questions.questionTextEn: The potential difference across a $2\ \mu\text{F}$ parallel-plate capacitor increases at a constant rate of $500\text{ V/s}$. The displacement current between the plates is ______ $\text{mA}$. (Answer in integer)
questions.explanationEn: The displacement current equals $I_d = C\frac{dV}{dt} = (2 \times 10^{-6})(500) = 1.0 \times 10^{-3}\text{ A} = 1\text{ mA}$.

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM PH Topic • Electricity and Magnetism (Set 02)
questions.questionTextEn: A plane electromagnetic wave traveling in vacuum has an electric field amplitude of $900\text{ V/m}$. Taking $c = 3 \times 10^8\text{ m/s}$, the magnetic field amplitude of the wave is ______ $\mu\text{T}$. (Answer in integer)
questions.explanationEn: In vacuum, $B_0 = \frac{E_0}{c} = \frac{900}{3 \times 10^8} = 3 \times 10^{-6}\text{ T} = 3\ \mu\text{T}$.

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM PH Topic • Electricity and Magnetism (Set 02)
questions.questionTextEn: A solid dielectric sphere carries a radial polarization $\vec{P}(r) = 3r^2\hat{r}\text{ C/m}^2$ (where $r$ is in meters). The bound volume charge density $\rho_b$ at $r = 0.5\text{ m}$ is ______ $\text{C/m}^3$. (Answer in integer)
questions.explanationEn: In spherical coordinates, $\rho_b = -\nabla\cdot\vec{P} = -\frac{1}{r^2}\frac{d}{dr}(r^2 P_r) = -\frac{1}{r^2}\frac{d}{dr}(3r^4) = -12r$. At $r = 0.5\text{ m}$, $\rho_b = -12(0.5) = -6\text{ C/m}^3$.
